o: The area between the demand curve and the price, up to the quantity bought
The area under the supply curve
why: Each buyer would have paid up to the demand curve but only paid the price. The gap, added up over all units, is the surplus.

q: Demand is P = 20 − Q and the price is 8. Find consumer surplus.
why: Subtract the price paid: ∫₀¹² (20 − Q − 8) dQ = 144 − 72 = 72, the triangle ½ · 12 · 12.

q: For a downward-sloping demand curve, a price rise lowers consumer surplus.
why: Fact. Buyers pay more for the units they still buy and give up some units, so both parts of the area shrink.

q: Marginal cost is MC = 2q. What is the extra cost of making the first 10 units (ignore fixed cost)?
why: Integrating a marginal gives a total: ∫₀¹⁰ 2q dq = q² from 0 to 10 = 100.

q: With no taxes or externalities, total surplus is largest at the market equilibrium.
why: Every unit whose value to buyers is above its cost gets traded, and no other units do.
